$\int {{{5\tan x} \over {\tan x - 2}}} dx = \int {{{5{{\sin x} \over {\cos x}}} \over {{{\sin x} \over {\cos x}} - 2}}} \,dx = \int {$\left( {{{5$\sin$ x} $\over$ {$\cos$ x}} \times {{$\cos$ x} $\over$ {$\sin$ x - 2$\cos$ x}}} \right)$} \,dx = \int {{{5\,\sin \,x\,dx} \over {\sin x - 2\,\cos x}}} = \int {$\left( {{{4$\sin$ x + $\sin$ x + 2$\cos$ x - 2$\cos$ x} $\over$ {$\sin$ x - 2$\cos$ x}}} \right)$} \,dx = \int {{{$\left( {$\sin$ x - 2$\cos$ x} \right) + \left( {4$\sin$ x + 2$\cos$ x} \right)$} \over {\sin x - 2\cos x}}} \,dx = \int {{{$\left( {$\sin$ x - 2$\cos$ x} \right)$ + 2$\left( {$\cos$ x + 2$\sin$ x} \right)$} \over {$\left( {$\sin$ x - 2$\cos$ x} \right)$}}} \,dx = \int {{{\sin x - 2\cos x} \over {\sin x - 2\cos x}}dx + 2\int {$\left( {{{$\cos$ x + 2$\sin$ x} $\over$ {$\sin$ x - 2$\cos$ x}}} \right)$} } \,dx = \int {dx + 2\int {{{\cos x + 2\sin x} \over {\sin x - 2\cos \,x}}} } \,dx = {I_1} + {I_2}$ where ${I_1} = \int {dx}$ and

${I_2} = 2\int {{{\cos x + 2\sin x} \over {\sin x - 2\cos x}}\,dx}$

Put $\sin x - 2\cos x = t  \Rightarrow$ \left( {$\cos$ x + 2$\sin$ x} \right)$dx = dt \therefore {I_2} = 2\int {{{dt} \over t}}  = 2\ln \,t + C = 2\, \ln$ \left( {$\sin$ \,x - 2$\cos$ \,x} \right)$ + C$
